label: Guesses at help syntax instead of using --help or man
description: The learner invents help commands like `doc cp` instead of checking `cp --help` or `man cp`.

remediation.explanation: Every command answers to `command --help` for a quick summary and `man command` for the full manual.

label: Mixes up absolute and relative paths
description: The learner treats a relative path like `reports/2026.md` as if it worked from any directory.

remediation.explanation: A path starting with / (or ~) is anchored from the top. Anything else starts from where you are.

label: Reads ~ as a literal folder name
description: The learner thinks `cd ~/projects` enters a folder literally named ~.

remediation.explanation: The shell expands ~ to your home directory before the command runs.

label: Expects ls to show hidden files
description: The learner does not realise files starting with a dot are hidden from plain ls.

remediation.explanation: A leading dot hides a file from plain `ls`. Add -a to see it.

label: Swaps head and tail
description: The learner uses head when they want the end of a file and tail when they want the start.

remediation.explanation: head reads from the top, tail reads from the bottom.

label: Picks the wrong wc flag
description: The learner confuses wc -l (lines) with -w (words) and -c (bytes).

remediation.explanation: l for lines, w for words, c for characters or bytes.

label: Swaps the grep pattern and file order
description: The learner writes `grep file.txt pattern` instead of `grep pattern file.txt`.

remediation.explanation: grep takes the pattern first, then the file: `grep pattern file`.

label: Uses a pipe where a redirect is needed
description: The learner writes `ls | list.txt` as if a pipe could name a file.

remediation.explanation: A pipe | connects two commands. A redirect > or >> connects a command to a file.

label: Overwrites when intending to append
description: The learner uses > when they wanted >> and destroys earlier content.

remediation.explanation: One > overwrites the file. Two >> append to the end.

label: Swaps cp and mv
description: The learner uses mv when they wanted a copy, or cp when they wanted to move.

remediation.explanation: cp copies and leaves the original. mv moves and removes the original, doubling as rename.

label: Copies directories without -r
description: The learner runs plain `cp` on a directory and gets an error or a partial copy.

remediation.explanation: cp copies single files. For a directory and everything inside it, add -r.

label: Omits the search path in find
description: The learner writes `find -name "*.log"` without the starting directory.

remediation.explanation: find always walks from a starting point: `find . -name "*.log"`.

label: Reaches for sudo by habit
description: The learner uses sudo for everyday commands, masking permission problems and raising risk.

remediation.explanation: sudo runs a command as root. Use it for admin tasks only, and ask why permission was denied first.

label: Believes rm is undoable
description: The learner thinks deleted files rest in a Trash folder and can be restored.

remediation.explanation: rm is permanent. There is no trash and no undo; only backups save you.
